questions.q: How do you reference a variable named varFileName in the User namespace inside an SSIS expression?
options: @[User::varFileName]
$User::varFileName
#varFileName
User.varFileName
questions.explain: Variables are referenced with an @ sign followed by the namespace, two colons, and the name — @[User::varFileName].

questions.q: What construct does the SSIS expression language use in place of an IF statement?
options: The conditional (ternary) operator: condition ? true_result : false_result
A CASE WHEN block, just like T-SQL
A Script Task is always required for any conditional logic
SWITCH()
questions.explain: SSIS expressions have no IF keyword — branching is done entirely with the ternary conditional operator, condition ? true : false.

questions.q: What does the cast (DT_WSTR, 30) do when placed in front of a value in an expression?
options: Converts the value to a 30-character-wide string so it can be concatenated or compared against other strings
Rounds a number to 30 decimal places
Truncates a string to its first 30 characters and discards the rest
Sets a 30-second timeout on the expression's evaluation
questions.explain: DT_WSTR is a Unicode string type cast; the number is the string's fixed width. Casting is necessary because SSIS's expression language is strict about mixing incompatible types.

questions.q: In the property expression DAY((DT_DBTIMESTAMP)GETDATE())==1||DAY((DT_DBTIMESTAMP)GETDATE())==15?1:2 used to set a package's LoggingMode, why does it use 1 and 2 instead of Enabled and Disabled?
options: A property expression that sets an enumerated property must use the enumerator's underlying numeric value, not its friendly name
1 and 2 are just arbitrary placeholder values with no real meaning
LoggingMode doesn't actually accept enumerator names at all, ever
Numeric values evaluate faster than named ones
questions.explain: When a property expression targets an enumerated property like LoggingMode, you must supply the enumeration's numeric equivalent (1 for Enabled, 2 for Disabled) rather than the friendly name shown in the UI.

questions.q: Which tool lets you drag variables and functions into an expression and see its evaluated result before committing to it?
options: The Expression Builder dialog
The Variables window's Grid Options
SQL Server Management Studio's Query Editor
The Package Explorer tab
questions.explain: The Expression Builder provides a Variables tree, function-family folders you can drag terms from, an Expression box, and an Evaluate Expression button to preview the real result.
